summary: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot() renamed every legacy session file over the destination path unconditionally, silently overwriting an existing session copy and deleting the legacy source. The migration now treats an existing destination as authoritative: it skips the colliding legacy file, leaving both copies byte-identical, and continues with the remaining files.

changes.change: In migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot(), before the renameSync(file, newPath) call, added an `if (existsSync(newPath)) continue;` guard replacing the fault-marker comment. No other production line changed.

claims.claim: The faulty production code is the session migration loop in migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot, which renames over an existing destination.
The repair is a single early-continue guard so an existing destination always wins and the legacy source stays in place.
The regression exercises the repaired production function through the read-only loader with a caller-owned temporary agentDir.
The collision assertions check destination bytes, legacy source bytes and continued migration of unrelated files.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root on Node v24.14.0 with no installed dependencies. The script loads the real packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs loadMigrations (real fs/path, faked getAgentDir/stripBom) and calls the exported migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot. Four scenarios assert behavior: (1) with a legacy ~/.pi/agent/sess.jsonl colliding with an existing sessions/<encoded-cwd>/sess.jsonl, the destination bytes are unchanged, the legacy source still exists with identical bytes, and an unrelated legacy session in the same pass is migrated with content preserved and its root copy gone; (2) running the migration twice leaves both copies stable (idempotent, including a Windows-style cwd encoding); (3) after a skipped collision, two further legacy files still migrate out of the agent root; (4) a non-colliding legacy session migrates normally. Falsifiability was verified by temporarily restoring the original faulty line (unconditional renameSync over the destination): the script then exited 1 with AssertionError 'existing destination must always win: its bytes must never be overwritten' (three scenarios failed), and after restoring the fix it exits 0 again. No stubs or printed-success shortcuts replace the assertions; all checks are assert calls from node:assert/strict, and temporary directories are created under .prale-eval/ and removed in a finally block. No optional validation dependency was missing, so no limitation applies.
